title: range() Start and Step
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know the start and step parts of range(), so you can count from any number and skip by a fixed jump.
learn: Use range(start, stop) to choose where counting begins
Use range(start, stop, step) to jump by a step
Count down with a negative step
idea: range() can take up to three numbers: start, stop, and step. range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3, 4, and it still stops before the stop value. range(0, 11, 2) jumps by 2, so you get 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. A negative step counts backwards, like range(5, 0, -1).
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the countdown from range(3, 0, -1) to range(5, 0, -1) and press Run. Go! should come after 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

practice.text: Print every multiple of 5 from 5 to 25 using range with a step.
practice.hint: The for line is already set up. Print n inside the loop and you will get 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.
practice.starterTip: Fill in print(n) on the indented line under for n in range(5, 26, 5):.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if output shows 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 using for with range and a step of 5.

practice.text: Finish the countdown from 5 to 1, then print Go!.
practice.hint: Inside the loop, print n for 5 down to 1. After the loop, back at the left edge with no extra indent, print Go!.
practice.starterTip: Use print(n) inside the for block, then print("Go!") on the last line. Not indented under for.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 5 through 1 print, then Go! (or similar) after the loop.

quiz.question: What does range(10, 0, -2) produce?
quiz.correct: Right, it starts at 10, steps down by 2, and stops before 0.
quiz.wrong: The stop is not included, so range(10, 0, -2) never reaches 0.

quiz.question: In range(1, 10, 2), what does the 2 mean?
quiz.correct: Yes, the third number is the step, which is how much to add each time.
quiz.wrong: In range(start, stop, step), the last number is the step size.

quiz.question: What numbers does range(2, 6) produce?
quiz.correct: Right, it starts at 2 and stops before 6.
quiz.wrong: range(start, stop) includes the start but not the stop.
